root.name: English Defense: Perrin Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 e6 2. c4 b6 3. e4 Bb7 4. Bd3 Nc6

overview: After 1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3, Black plays 4...Nc6 and aims to attack the large White centre with ...Nb4, ...Bb4+ and ...f5. White builds with Ne2, Nc3 and f3 or tries to punish the loosely placed pieces. The game is double-edged: White has the space, Black has the counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Ne2, Nc3 and O-O

black_ideas.idea: Pressure d4 and e4 with ...Nb4, ...Bb4+ and ...Bb7
Make use of the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Big White centre under hypermodern attack

character.notes: Black's setup is double-edged, with tactics around the White centre.

gambit.notes: No material given at the root.

soundness.notes: Playable but gives White the space and centre; theory rates it as fine for both.

structure.notes: The White pawn centre is attacked by pieces and pawn breaks, so it is not locked.

approach.notes: Strong players do play the English Defence now and then.

level.notes: Black must understand the hypermodern counterplay.

character.reason: The parent English Defence is double-edged and 4...Nc6 gives both sides real attacking chances.

gambit.reason: No material has been offered at the root.

soundness.reason: Black's counter-pressure is respectable and not refuted.

structure.reason: The centre is in tension, with White's pawns attacked by pieces.

approach.reason: The English Defence is an occasional choice of strong players.

level.reason: Black needs to know the typical breaks but there is not a lot of forced theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre and attacks it from the flank.
